implementation_notes: Kotlin/Android's framework-native equivalent is MVI rather than a store singleton: a ViewModel owns a MutableStateFlow<UiState>, receives intents through a reduce(state, intent) function, emits immutable data-class states, and the UI collects them with collectAsStateWithLifecycle; one-shot effects go through a SharedFlow/Channel and asynchronous work runs in viewModelScope. This replaces the dispatcher/store plumbing with one state holder per screen plus structured concurrency, which is why the language is classified idiomatic; choose the redux-kotlin variant when a single application-wide store with middleware and time travel is genuinely required.
pitfalls: StateFlow conflates equal consecutive values, so a state whose fields are also equal drops the emission; model one-shot events separately (SharedFlow/Channel) instead of pushing them through state.
Writing to _state from several coroutines without a single reduce path recreates the races MVI removes; funnel every change through update { reduce(...) }.
A ViewModel that outlives the screen keeps resources alive: avoid Context/View references and use viewModelScope so work is cancelled with the owner.
Collecting the flow without the lifecycle (plain collect in an effect, or collectAsState in older Compose) keeps updating an inactive UI.

variants.name: ReduxKotlin store (multiplatform Redux port)
variants.implementation_notes: ReduxKotlin is a Kotlin Multiplatform port of Redux - 'a predictable state container for Kotlin apps' with, by design, the same API as JavaScript Redux - so the classic store/reducer/middleware structure is available unchanged across JVM, Native, JS and WASM, with extensions for thunks, Jetpack Compose bindings and presenter middleware. It is the choice when the shared store must span targets or when the team already reasons in Redux terms; for a single Android screen the MVI variant with ViewModel and StateFlow reaches the same one-way flow with framework primitives and no extra dependency.
pitfalls: A single global store shared across multiplatform targets must not hold platform types (Android Context, iOS handles) or the state stops being serializable and the targets stop being interchangeable.
Middleware ordering decides whether an action is logged before or after reducers run; inconsistent ordering between targets makes replay behaviour diverge.
Subscribers registered from a screen must be unsubscribed with the screen's lifecycle, or the store keeps the screen (and its views) alive.
